newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Goodman Fielder welcomes Defiance approval.
newsitem.headline: Goodman Fielder welcomes Defiance approval.

text.p: Goodman Fielder Ltd said on Tuesday it welcomed a regulator's decision to approve its acquisition of the New Zealand baking and milling assets of Defiance Food Industries Ltd.

Goodman Fielder said the decision by New Zealand's Commerce Commission meant it would sell its Champion flour mill in Christchurch to a unit of George Weston Foods Ltd, to ensure effective competition continued.

"We are pleased that the Commerce Commission had approved our revised application because of the benefits to customers from a more comprehensive and efficient national service," Goodman's chief executive David Hearn.
Hearn said the acquisition would be a key plank in Goodman's plans to improve internal efficiency.
The Commerce Commission rejected Goodman's NZ$48 million bid to buy the Defiance assets on April 14 due to the potential for Goodman to become a dominant force in N.Z. markets.
Goodman lodged a revised application in late May, offering to sell the Champion mill to meet the commission's concerns about the size of the combined businesses.
Both Goodman Fielder and Defiance are based in Australia and have extensive interests in New Zealand.
George Weston, which is also Australian-based, is 78 percent owned by Associated British Foods Plc.

The plan to sell the Defiance assets in New Zealand coincided with a takeover bid for Defiance by South American food group Bunge, which took control of the Queensland-based company on May 16 after raising its bid a number of times.
